name: S2ORC
data_summary: S2ORC means Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus. It aggregates research metadata and machine-readable academic text, including citation and figure/table mentions, across publishers and archives. The original 2020 release reported 81.1M paper records, with structured full text for 8.1M open-access papers; those are historical snapshot counts, not current availability. It is a corpus, not an OCR model. Original S2ORC paper

name: peS2o
data_summary: peS2o is an already cleaned and packaged language-model corpus derived from S2ORC and Semantic Scholar abstracts. Its v2 training split lists 8,242,162 full-text-derived records and 30,569,017 title/abstract-derived records. Thus, approximately 39M documents must not be described as 39M full-text papers. Its full-text branch uses GROBID-derived text and removes figures, tables and references. This saves extraction/curation work for text training but cannot replace source assets for our multimodal records. Author documentation and exact split counts

name: Dolma
data_summary: The original Dolma corpus reports Common Crawl 2,479B; GitHub 411B; Reddit 89B; Semantic Scholar/peS2o 70B; Gutenberg 6B; Wikipedia/Wikibooks 4.3B, approximately 3,059B total with its stated tokenizer. This is a reusable dataset's composition, not a biology-only training run or the later Dolma 3 mix. Its academic component can be selected for biology; that selected amount is not given by the 70B headline. Original Dolma, Table 1 / §8
